report_meta.report_title: Web Application Security Audit of the Citizen Services Portal

audit_certificate.statement: The application, its backend databases and scripts were found free from known exploitable vulnerabilities and malicious code as on the date of revalidation.

assets.in_scope_functions: Citizen login, application submission, admin dashboard for officer and admin roles
REST API used by the portal for user and admin operations

inaccessible_assets.reason: Module decommissioned by the auditee during the engagement

scope_categories.reason: Source code not provided by the auditee
Hosting provider assessed under a separate audit

secure_design_confirmation.statement: The auditee confirmed by letter dated 28 June 2026 that the portal was developed following the CERT-In application security guidelines.

methodology.narrative: The portal (asset 1) and its API gateway (asset 2) were tested in production against OWASP WSTG test cases for authentication, session management, input validation and business logic, and against ASVS level 2 requirements. The legacy reports module (asset 3) was excluded after decommissioning.
methodology.manual_testing: Manual testing of authentication, authorisation between citizen, officer and admin roles, and business logic of the application submission workflow using an intercepting proxy.
methodology.automated_testing: Automated scanning with Burp Suite Professional and Nmap, with all scanner findings manually confirmed.
methodology.sampling_decisions: All 46 citizen-facing functions were tested; officer functions were sampled at 60 per cent, prioritising those that modify application status.
methodology.prioritisation_approach: Functions handling personal data and payment references were tested first.
limitations: Testing windows were restricted to 22:00 to 06:00 on production.
Source code was not made available.

severity_scheme.description: Severity follows the CVSS v3.1 qualitative rating.

tools_ipr_license_confirmation.statement: All tools used are licensed or open source and used in accordance with their licences.

executive_summary.narrative: The audit found two high-risk weaknesses. A flaw in how citizen applications are retrieved allowed one citizen to read another citizen's application, exposing personal data. An outdated web server component could allow an attacker to read files from the server. Both have been fixed and verified. One low-risk weakness remains open.

overall_security_posture.description: After remediation the portal is in a moderate security posture; one low-risk issue remains.

executive_summary.business_risk_summary: Before remediation, personal data of all citizens could have been exposed, with legal and reputational consequences under the DPDP Act.
key_recommendations: Retain object-level authorisation checks in the API (owner: application team, by 30 September 2026)
Adopt a monthly patch cycle for web server components (owner: hosting team)

summary_table.title: Insecure direct object reference in application retrieval
Path traversal in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.49

detailed_observations.title: Insecure direct object reference in application retrieval
detailed_observations.severity_rationale: Network reachable without user interaction; any authenticated citizen can read other citizens' applications, so confidentiality impact is high. Privileges were scored as none because self-registration is open to anyone.
detailed_observations.observation_description: The endpoint GET /v1/applications/{id} returns the application of any citizen when the numeric identifier is changed, without verifying that the application belongs to the requesting user.
detailed_observations.preconditions: A citizen account, obtainable through open self-registration.

proof_of_concept.reference: GET /v1/applications/10452 HTTP/1.1 (session of citizen A) -> 200 OK, body contains name and Aadhaar-masked number of citizen B
proof_of_concept.description: Request with citizen A's session token for citizen B's application, captured in Burp Suite.

proof_of_concept.reference: GET /v1/applications/10452 HTTP/1.1 (session of citizen A) -> 403 Forbidden
proof_of_concept.description: Retest after fix: the same request is refused.

detailed_observations.impact: Disclosure of personal data of every citizen with an application on the portal.
detailed_observations.likely_root_cause: Authorisation is enforced only at the user interface; the API does not check ownership of the object requested.
detailed_observations.recommendation: Enforce an ownership check in the applications service so that GET /v1/applications/{id} compares the application's owner identifier with the authenticated subject, and return 403 otherwise; apply the same check to all object-level endpoints (ASVS V4.2.1, WSTG-ATHZ-04).

detailed_observations.title: Path traversal in Apache HTTP Server 2.4.49
detailed_observations.observation_description: The portal runs Apache HTTP Server 2.4.49, in which a crafted URL with encoded dot segments maps to files outside the document root.
detailed_observations.preconditions: None; the server is reachable from the internet.

proof_of_concept.description: Traversal request returns the server host name.

detailed_observations.impact: Disclosure of files readable by the web server and, where CGI is enabled, remote code execution.
detailed_observations.likely_root_cause: Web server component not patched since 2021.
detailed_observations.recommendation: Upgrade Apache HTTP Server to 2.4.51 or later (2.4.62 recommended) and set 'Require all denied' on the root directory.

detailed_observations.title: Missing Content-Security-Policy header
detailed_observations.severity_rationale: Exploitation requires a separate injection flaw and user interaction; impact is limited to partial disclosure.
detailed_observations.observation_description: Responses from the portal do not include a Content-Security-Policy header, so the browser applies no restriction on script sources.
detailed_observations.preconditions: A separate script injection flaw and a victim who opens a crafted page.

proof_of_concept.description: Response headers of the home page captured with Burp Suite.

detailed_observations.impact: Increases the impact of any script injection.
detailed_observations.likely_root_cause: Security headers not configured in the reverse proxy.
detailed_observations.recommendation: Add a Content-Security-Policy header in the reverse proxy configuration restricting script-src to 'self' and the portal's CDN, starting in report-only mode for two weeks.
